thought.text: The user's home dir `/opt/elasticsearch` (created by `useradd -m`) blocked the move. I'll keep the install at `/opt/elasticsearch-7.17.28` and symlink to it.

reasoning_content:
`useradd -r -m` created /opt/elasticsearch as the home directory of the elastic user before the mv. The shell glob `elasticsearch-7.17.28/*` — wait, `mv /opt/elasticsearch/elasticsearch-7.17.28 /opt/elasticsearch` — since the target exists as a directory, mv moved the nested directory inside it… actually, in the first failed attempt, `mv /opt/downloads/elasticsearch-7.17.28 /opt/elasticsearch` placed it at `/opt/elasticsearch/elasticsearch-7.17.28` (because /opt/elasticsearch already existed as the home directory). Then, the second attempt's `mv /opt/elasticsearch/elasticsearch-7.17.28 /opt/elasticsearch-7.17.28` was… wait, this second mv: the source is /opt/elasticsearch/elasticsearch-7.17.28 (the nested one), and the target /opt/elasticsearch-7.17.28 doesn't exist → it should move cleanly. After that, rmdir /opt/elasticsearch failed because it contains dotfiles (the home files). Looking at the listing, the current state is: /opt/elasticsearch-7.17.28 has the full ES tree, and /opt/elasticsearch contains only the dotfiles (the home). The symlink was not created (rmdir failed → && chain halted).

The simplest approach: leave /opt/elasticsearch as the user's home directory (which is fine), and put the ES installation at /opt/elasticsearch-7.17.28, with a /opt/es symlink pointing there. Update the yml paths accordingly.

action.command:
ln -sfn /opt/elasticsearch-7.17.28 /opt/es && cat > /opt/elasticsearch-7.17.28/config/elasticsearch.yml <<'EOF'
cluster.name: index-data-explorer
node.name: node-1
path.data: /opt/elasticsearch-7.17.28/data
path.logs: /opt/elasticsearch-7.17.28/logs
network.host: 127.0.0.1
http.port: 9200
discovery.type: single-node
EOF
chown elastic:elastic /opt/elasticsearch-7.17.28/config/elasticsearch.yml && /opt/es/bin/elasticsearch --version | head -1 && echo CONFIG_OK
